rows.what the ink shows: A heavily retraced upright before the opening parenthesis has an upper return, a middle arm and a lower hooked end. Overlapping closed-looking compartments prevent securely separating E from a B-like underform.
The sequence has the small looped d and low ans, a separate tall l with low a, then a tall d and long compressed deuxième with its raised accent and dotted i.
After la, a long heavy horizontal cancellation covers the word bodies. A small central hump and a short raised remnant remain, but no recoverable letter sequence distinguishes a word.
The inserted word above the deletion starts with a tall hooked t/r gesture, followed by a low rounded join and a detached trailing ce stroke. Its compact joined shape supports trace.
The f has a tall descending entry and rising return; two dots sit over the following compressed low strokes, with a short final e before the comma.
A rounded initial a joins a tall looped l, followed by a low o/r sequence and a right-hooking final s before the closing parenthesis.
Between 1 and A there is one short horizontal stroke with a thickened right tip and no vertical crossing. The nearby plus in the right-hand subscript has a distinct crossing upright.

The open O and joined n, low est, ramené opening r/a and raised final accent, detached à, and the long p descender of prouver survive the sloping deletion. Several interior joins lie under the cancellation.

Two baseline glyphs are visible: a retraced triangular Delta and a separate B with an upright and two right bowls. The lower overlapping strokes stay within these glyphs; no distinct raised or lowered index is visible.
The sign has a thick, roughly rectangular upper horizontal bar and a separate lower parallel bar. The left edge is overfilled but does not preserve a distinct open angle.

Tr has a high sweeping T cap and a small following r. The last baseline capital has a pointed sloping outline and projecting cross-stroke suggestive of A, but dense retracing also conceals possible E arms.
The small marginal deletion above Nous is crossed by a long heavy line; only a short downward hook, a dot and a thick low tail remain below it. They do not form a secure readable word.
